description: Cabreuva is a hard, heavy, aromatic South American hardwood with reddish to purplish-brown heartwood. In Europe it has mainly been used for parquet and other flooring.

hazards.summary: A parquet floor layer had a delayed asthma attack when challenged with cabreuva dust in hospital, while a control challenge with fir dust was negative. A later case report describes rhinitis and asthma from the same wood.
In the same patient, the hospital challenge with cabreuva dust also caused fever, vomiting, and muscle aches. Such whole-body reactions to wood dust appear to be rare.
An inflammatory lung reaction (allergic alveolitis) has been reported after exposure to cabreuva dust. How the diagnosis was confirmed could not be checked.
All wood dust, including cabreuva, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed cabreuva (Myrocarpus fastigiatus) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Rich reddish-brown to purplish-brown heartwood with darker variegated streaks, and a narrow band of yellowish-white sapwood along one edge. Fine, even texture with interlocked grain, a slightly oily surface, and a high natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.

notes_internal: Systemic_toxic set to level 1 because the reaction was reproduced during a bronchial provocation test (single patient; patient declined further study). Pala-2010 and Baur-2000 have no abstracts. Trade name 'cabreuva' is also used for Myrocarpus frondosus and Myroxylon peruiferum in some markets - which species the patients handled was taken from paper titles only. Common name 'oleo pardo' from general trade usage, unsourced - verify or remove. Name checked on GBIF only. No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
